fact: The Association of Shelter Veterinarians' standards of care say gravel, dirt and grass surfaces cannot be disinfected, and that surface covers such as pea gravel can be replaced or recovered regularly to cut the contaminant load.
quote: Outdoor areas around the shelter must be kept clean, recognizing it is impossible to disinfect gravel, dirt, and grass surfaces. … Surface covers (e.g. pea gravel, mulch, and rubber chips) can be replaced or recovered regularly to reduce contaminant load.
source_label: Association of Shelter Veterinarians, Guidelines for Standards of Care in Animal Shelters, 2nd ed. (2022), section 5.5, Other shelter areas
notes: Read in the full PDF of the guidelines hosted by ASPCApro (the guidelines' DOI, 10.56771/ASVguidelines.2022, resolves to jsmcah.org). The reference numeral after 'grass surfaces.' is left out of the quote. Written for shelters: the page applies it to a home dog run by analogy and says the standard is a shelter's.

fact: The same shelter standards call daily removal of feces from outdoor areas acceptable and immediate removal preferred, to keep parasite eggs from building up.
quote: Feces must be removed from outdoor areas between animals or groups. … To reduce parasite egg accumulation in the environment, daily removal of feces is acceptable, although immediate removal is preferred.
source_label: Association of Shelter Veterinarians, Guidelines for Standards of Care in Animal Shelters, 2nd ed. (2022), section 5.5, Other shelter areas
notes: Reference numerals in the source are left out of the quote.

fact: The Companion Animal Parasite Council says roundworm eggs are hardy and long-lived, common disinfectants do not kill them, and once they are in the ground only extreme measures such as paving the area, removing the topsoil, burning or steam get rid of them.
quote: Removing eggs from a contaminated environment is difficult, and common disinfectants are not effective at killing them. … Treating pets to prevent egg shedding is critical because the eggs are very hardy and long-lived in the environment. Once present, the eggs can be removed or destroyed only through extreme measures such as paving kennel areas or areas of pet defecation with concrete or asphalt, complete removal of topsoil, prescribed burns, or treatment with steam.
source_label: Companion Animal Parasite Council, Ascarid guidelines (dog)

fact: CAPC says most roundworm eggs need 2 to 4 weeks in the environment to become infective, and that prompt removal of feces from the yard keeps eggs from staying behind as the feces break down.
quote: Most ascarid eggs require 2 to 4 weeks in the environment to larvate and develop to the infective stage. … Prompt removal of feces from the yard or the litterbox will also help prevent ascarid eggs from remaining in the environment as the fecal material decomposes or is dispersed.
source_label: Companion Animal Parasite Council, Ascarid guidelines (dog)

fact: CSU Extension's PlantTalk Colorado counts pea gravel among the inorganic mulches and says inorganic mulches store and radiate heat, so large areas of unshaded rock should not go next to a house.
quote: Inorganic mulches are stone-based and include rock, cobblestone, pea gravel, lava rock and crushed rock. … Inorganic mulches also store and radiate heat, so avoid putting large areas of unshaded rock next to a house.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado 1905, Xeriscape Mulches

fact: CSU Extension says pea gravel improves water infiltration into the soil, especially during short, intense storms such as thunderstorms.
quote: Pea gravel has been shown to improve water infiltration into the soil, especially in short, intense precipitation events like thunderstorms; larger rocks increase runoff.

fact: Toro's operator's manual for its Power Clear snowthrower says the machine is designed mainly for paved surfaces and is not designed for clearing gravel surfaces.
quote: It is designed primarily for removing snow from paved surfaces, such as driveways and sidewalks, and other surfaces for traffic on residential or commercial properties. It is not designed for removing materials other than snow, nor is it designed for clearing gravel surfaces.
source_label: Toro, Power Clear 721 R/E Snowthrower operator's manual (Model Nos. 38741 and 38742)
notes: The same 'not designed for clearing gravel surfaces' sentence appears in Toro's Power Clear 518 and SnowMaster 724/824 QXE manuals (manuals.toro.com/132080 and /257357), read the same day.

fact: VCA Animal Hospitals says a dog with pica may eat rocks and other non-food items, and that the most common problem pica causes is a gastrointestinal obstruction.
quote: Pica is a condition where a dog persistently ingests non-food items. For example, they may eat plastic, paper, fabric, sticks, rocks, or mulch. … The most common problem that pica causes is gastrointestinal obstruction due to a non-digestible object getting stuck in the esophagus, stomach, or intestines.
source_label: VCA Animal Hospitals, Pica in Dogs (Krista Williams, DVM)
